text: Using Grok AI
A short course on getting useful answers from Grok.
What Grok is
Grok is an AI assistant built by xAI. It answers questions, writes code, searches the web, and can run tools on your behalf.
It is not a search engine and not a calculator. It is a conversation.
Ask a specific question
Vague prompts get vague answers. Tell Grok what you want, who it is for, and what done looks like.
Weak: 'Tell me about Python.'
Better: 'Write a 10-line Python function that reads a CSV and prints the sum of the second column.'
Give context and constraints
Include the pieces Grok cannot guess: your language, your file format, the error you saw, the length you want.
If you have a file, say so. If you want a table, say so. If you want code that runs, say so.
Use tools when the answer is not in the model
Grok can search the web, open pages, run code, and talk to services you connect.
Ask it to check a current fact, run a snippet, or look at a file you point it at. Do not ask it to invent numbers it can look up.
Iterate
The first answer is a draft. Tell Grok what is wrong or missing and ask for a revision.
Short corrections work: 'Make it shorter', 'Use the existing function names', 'That number is from 2022, check again.'
Check the work
Grok can be wrong. For anything that matters, verify the output yourself or ask Grok to show its source.
Code should be run. Numbers should be checked. Quotes should be traced.
Done
Ask clearly, give context, use tools, iterate, and check.
That is the whole course.
